title: Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading: dual listings and the Global Listing Board
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by Mr Chee Hong Tat on behalf of the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, that introduces a framework for dual listings between SGX and eligible overseas exchanges and makes other amendments to the Securities and Futures Act.
why_it_matters: The Bill is intended to let issuers use one prospectus and harmonised rules to list concurrently on SGX and an overseas exchange, starting with the Global Listing Board with Nasdaq, and to reduce compliance costs. It also allows issuers to engage retail investors using preliminary prospectuses, subject to safeguards, and clarifies that the company issuing underlying shares, not the depositary, lodges the prospectus for depositary receipt offerings. The record says investors will also gain access to a broader range of high-quality investment opportunities and that Singapore investors will continue to be able to seek recourse for losses arising from such breaches under the investor recourse provisions in the SFA.

key_points.point: The Bill introduces a new legislative framework to facilitate dual listing arrangements on SGX.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: The Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill introduces a new legislative framework to facilitate dual listing arrangements on the Singapore Exchange (SGX)

key_points.point: The Global Listing Board provides issuers a direct pathway to access capital across both markets with one prospectus and harmonised rules.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: The GLB provides issuers a direct pathway to access capital across both markets with one prospectus and a harmonised set of rules.

key_points.point: The Equity Market Development Programme will allocate up to $6.5 billion directly and crowd in private capital.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: the Equity Market Development Programme, which will allocate up to $6.5 billion directly and also to crowd in private capital

key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: Trading volumes in the first quarter of 2026 rose 32% from the previous quarter to $126 billion, and the volumes in March were the highest in almost 20 years.

key_points.point: The Straits Times Index has risen by over 20% over the past year and over 100% over a five-year period.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: The Straits Times Index has risen by over 20% over the past year and over 100% over a five-year period

key_points.point: The first set of amendments introduces a new Part 13A to the SFA to support dual listing arrangements such as the GLB.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: the first set of amendments introduces a new Part 13A to the SFA. This provides a framework to support dual listing arrangements, such as the GLB.

key_points.point: A dual listing arrangement requires the overseas exchange to be from a jurisdiction with securities laws consistent with IOSCO international standards and principles.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: the overseas exchange is from a jurisdiction with securities laws consistent with the International Organisation of Securities Commissions' (IOSCO) international standards and principles

key_points.point: MAS can set regulations to modify offer-related provisions to facilitate a single set of offer documents.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: enabling MAS to set regulations to modify offer-related provisions to facilitate the use of a single set of offer documents.

key_points.point: MAS will align Singapore's listing timeline with that of the US by varying provisions relating to the prospectus registration process.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: MAS will align Singapore's listing timeline with that of the US by varying provisions relating to the prospectus registration process.

key_points.point: The Bill will enable MAS to set regulations to adopt safe harbours as defences to the market misconduct provisions in the SFA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: The Bill will enable MAS to set regulations to adopt safe harbours as defences to the market misconduct provisions in the SFA.

key_points.point: The safe harbours do not provide a valid defence against criminal liability for fraud or dishonest conduct.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: They do not provide a valid defence against criminal liability for fraud or dishonest conduct.

key_points.point: Issuers will be allowed to engage retail investors based on preliminary prospectuses rather than only using final prospectuses.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: issuers will be allowed to engage retail investors based on preliminary prospectuses rather than only using the final prospectuses.

key_points.point: Safeguards include that no offers can be made on the basis of the preliminary prospectus and the document must state its content is subject to further changes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: no offers can be made on the basis of the preliminary prospectus, and the document must also state clearly that its content is subject to further changes.

key_points.point: The Bill clarifies that the company issuing the underlying shares, not the financial institution acting as intermediary, must lodge the prospectus for registration for DR offerings.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: the Bill clarifies that it should be the company issuing the underlying shares that is the entity required to lodge its prospectus for registration, instead of the financial institution that acts as an intermediary when issuing the DRs.
